name: Bakumpai
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Ibrahim, Sjahrial S. A. R., Darmansyah & Durdje Durasid. 1979. Bahasa Bakumpai. (Pusat Bahasa grammar sketch, 131pp; per Glottolog). Kemdikbud repository unreachable (DNS dead); no other copy found.

sources.citation: Santoso, Dewi Mulyani et al. 1991. Struktur bahasa Dayak Ngaju. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Treats Bakumpai explicitly as one of three Ngaju dialects and discusses phonological differences; a stress statement for Ngaju dialects incl. Bakumpai is plausible. Pusat Bahasa PDF probably on the same (currently unreachable) repository.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 / 5.3 languoid baku1263 and our access check record for Ibrahim et al. 1979
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only one descriptive reference (Ibrahim et al. 1979); HathiTrust record 006195072 search-only; no Harvard copy.

sources.citation: Hasby, Qalyubi & Misrita. 2025. Perbandingan linguistik historis bahasa Dayak Ngaju dan Bakumpai. JBSI 5(1). doi:10.47709/jbsi.v5i01.5810
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexical/sound-correspondence comparison Ngaju vs Bakumpai; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Arief, Nur Fajar. 2019. Phonological process in passive verb markers of Bahasa Bakumpai. PAROLE: Journal of Linguistics and Education 9(2): 101-110. doi:10.14710/parole.v9i2.101-110
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Assimilation and syllable-structure processes with in-/-in- passives; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Jamzaroh, Siti. 2019. Refleks fonem PAN pada bahasa Bakumpai. Metalingua 17(2): 189-198. doi:10.26499/metalingua.v17i2.415
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 2.2.1 summarises Suryadikara et al. (1989-1990: 14): 4 vowels, [e] as [ɛ], marginal schwa from Banjar, diphthongs /ay aw uy ɛy/, 18 consonants; 'penultima' is used only for word position in reflexes. Silent on stress. Names Suryadikara et al. 1990 'Fonologi Bahasa Bakumpai' (Banjarmasin) and Yayuk 2009 thesis as its sources.

sources.citation: Ibrahim, Sjahrial S. A. R., Wini Tarmini & Maria Lusia Anita Sumaryati. 1995. Kamus Bahasa Indonesia-Bakumpai I. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. 209 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Front matter pp. vii-viii ('Aspek kebahasaan bahasa Bakumpai', explicitly following Ibrahim et al. 1979) lists 4 vowels /a i u e/, consonants and diphthongs /ai au eu ei ui/ and affixes; nothing on stress (tekanan) or any suprasegmental.

sources.citation: Kawi, Djantera. 1985. Kamus Bakumpai-Indonesia. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. 146 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pusat Bahasa dictionaries carry a short phonology/orthography introduction that sometimes notes stress; digital copy exists on the unreachable repository (eprint 1968), not archived by the Internet Archive.

sources.citation: Hudson, Alfred B. 1967. The Barito Isolects of Borneo: A Classification Based on Comparative Reconstruction and Lexicostatistics. Cornell SEAP Data Paper 68.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Full text (eCommons transcription) has no 'stress'/'accent' statement for any isolect; Bakumpai is mentioned only ethnographically (p. 4) as a Ngaju dialect; 'penultimate' occurs only in a note on vowel reflexes (p. 49).
